title: Projects
headline: Practical AI automations, built with Claude
lead: I'm a data analyst, not a developer. These projects turn everyday information overload into short, useful emails and pages that run on their own.
subtitle: Practical AI automations built with Claude as a coding partner. This page refreshes itself every week.

principles.title: Code in charge
principles.text: Ordinary code controls every step. The model is called only for specific jobs, like ranking, summarizing and extracting dates.

principles.title: Runs itself
principles.text: Everything runs on a schedule in the cloud. There's no server to maintain and no computer that has to stay on.

principles.title: Trust, but verify
principles.text: Model output is checked before it's used. For example, links come from the original email, not from the model.

principles.title: Private by design
principles.text: Credentials live in encrypted secrets, and personal details are kept out of the code and off this page.

glossary.definition: A pipeline where ordinary code controls every step (fetching, filtering, formatting, sending) and calls a large language model only for specific jobs such as ranking, summarizing or extracting dates. The model doesn't choose what happens next or use tools on its own, which keeps the result predictable and inexpensive. It differs from an agent, where the model itself directs the steps.

projects.name: Daily Reads
projects.tagline: A curated daily email of things worth reading.
projects.problem: Good reading gets buried across feeds, newsletters and an overflowing inbox.
projects.approach: Every morning a scheduled job gathers articles from RSS feeds, a personal source list and newsletters in Gmail. Claude ranks them and writes a short blurb for each of the best five. Ordinary code then adds the weather, upcoming dates found in the inbox, and one-click calendar buttons.
projects.outcome: One short email instead of checking many sources, with a reminder of what's coming up.

projects.name: School Update
projects.tagline: A daily digest of school emails, filtered to what applies.
projects.problem: Important notices are buried in long school newsletters, and dates are easy to miss.
projects.approach: Claude reads the emails in a Gmail label, keeps only what applies to the family, and sorts it into needs-action, coming-up and news, pulling out dates, times and links. Ordinary code turns each date into a one-click calendar event and sends only when something is relevant.
projects.outcome: A brief, action-first email with the right links and calendar buttons, and nothing at all on quiet days.

projects.name: Assignment Dashboard
projects.tagline: Every assignment across all courses, in one color-coded page.
projects.problem: Assignments and events are spread across many courses, so it's hard to see what's due next.
projects.approach: A Python script reads the Canvas learning platform API, ranks work by urgency, builds a filterable color-coded page, publishes it behind a password on GitHub Pages, and sends an evening digest.
projects.outcome: One page and one email that show everything due, running unattended in the cloud.

projects.name: Analytics Debugger
projects.tagline: A DevTools panel that makes web-analytics requests readable.
projects.problem: Analytics tracking requests are hard to read in raw network logs.
projects.approach: A Chrome extension captures the requests as a page loads and lays them out in a readable panel inside the browser's developer tools.
projects.outcome: Faster checking that analytics tracking is firing correctly.
projects.runs: Runs in the browser while debugging

projects.name: Writing
projects.tagline: Notes on building with AI as a non-developer.
projects.problem: Many people who understand data assume that building software isn't for them.
projects.approach: Sharing the process: a LinkedIn entry and a Medium article about going from an idea to a working, automated app with Claude as a coding partner.
projects.outcome: Practical notes for other analysts who want to build.
